scope: C1.2–C1.4 only; C1.1 retains its authored delivery_controls

C1.2-P1-M01.focus: Introduce sender, channel and receiver while showing that a bit sequence travels between them.
critical_checks: Identifies sender, channel and receiver and the sent bits.

C1.2-P1-M02.focus: Work one during-transmission bit flip with a clear sent/received comparison.
critical_checks: Identifies the change at 1-based position 3, from 1 to 0 during transmission.
Notes a bit flip can also be from 0 to 1.

C1.2-P1-M03.focus: Explain the difference between an instructor seeing two sequences and a real receiver seeing only what arrived.
critical_checks: Does not imply the receiver ordinarily has the clean original.

C1.2-P1-M04.focus: Conclude briefly why a receiver needs a way to check for possible changed bits.
critical_checks: Connects the receiver limitation to the need for detection.

C1.2-P2-M01.focus: Supply sender/channel/receiver terms directly before guided comparisons.
C1.2-P2-M01.avoid: No novice guessing or required question.
critical_checks: Supplies all three communication roles.

C1.2-P2-M02.focus: Ask the learner to locate the different bit between sent and received sequences; then explain the flip.
C1.2-P2-M02.avoid: Do not reveal position 3 or the changed symbol before the learner replies.
critical_checks: Question precedes revealing the changed position.
After a learner reply, verifies 1 to 0 at position 3 and mentions both flip directions.
C1.2-P2-M02.guided_question: Sent bits are `10110` and received bits are `10010`. Which position changed?

C1.2-P2-M03.focus: Guide which sequence an actual receiver can inspect and contrast with the instructor view.
C1.2-P2-M03.avoid: Do not give away the receiver-only perspective before the learner replies.
critical_checks: Question precedes answer.
Explains that receiver ordinarily has only the received bits, not the clean original.
C1.2-P2-M03.guided_question: We can see both sequences here. Which one would the receiver normally have?

C1.2-P2-M04.focus: If a learner earlier claimed the receiver already knows the original, correct that; otherwise briefly reaffirm without another question.
C1.2-P2-M04.avoid: Conditional move: do not invent a misconception or require a new learner response.
critical_checks: No extra guided question.
Corrects a receiver-has-original misconception if actually expressed.

C1.2-P2-M05.focus: Finish the short chain: sender to receiver, flip during transmission, receiver lacks original, so checking helps.
C1.2-P2-M05.avoid: Do not retell the full example or add a quiz.
critical_checks: Connects transmission changes and receiver limitation to detection.

C1.2-P3-M01.focus: Introduce a send/receive comparison with an unchanged case and a one-bit-changed case.
critical_checks: Compares same sent bits in intact and corrupted examples.
Names the changed bit at position 3 as transmission corruption.

C1.2-P3-M02.focus: Compare what stays fixed across the cases and what the receiver gets.
critical_checks: Sender, channel and sent bits are held fixed; only received position 3 differs.

C1.2-P3-M03.focus: Contrast an outside instructor who sees the original and the receiver who does not.
critical_checks: Explains information difference and lack of direct original comparison.

C1.2-P3-M04.focus: Draw the need for a checking method from the receiver-perspective contrast.
C1.2-P3-M04.avoid: No new question or repeated case walkthrough.
critical_checks: Links no clean original to the reason for error detection.

C1.3-P1-M01.focus: Use the receiver limitation from the previous subsection to motivate extra checking information.
critical_checks: Connects no original to the usefulness of checking information.

C1.3-P1-M02.focus: Show the original payload and a separate symbolic position p, defining the added position as redundancy and parity-bit location.
critical_checks: Identifies original payload separately from extra checking position.
Explains p is placeholder, not literal sent character or calculated bit.

C1.3-P1-M03.focus: Explain why the extra parity-bit value is determined from the original data by an agreed rule.
critical_checks: Distinguishes rule-based choice from arbitrary choice without calculating p.

C1.3-P1-M04.focus: Explain why sender and receiver must use the same rule; save even/odd calculations for later.
critical_checks: Both sides must agree on the checking rule; no concrete parity-bit calculation.

C1.3-P2-M01.focus: Explain directly why extra checking information might help a receiver without the original.
critical_checks: Explains receiver limitation and checking motivation.

C1.3-P2-M02.focus: Ask the learner to identify original payload versus the extra symbolic checking position.
C1.3-P2-M02.avoid: Do not supply the payload-versus-redundancy answer before the question; p is a placeholder.
critical_checks: Learner is asked to distinguish original payload from extra position.
After reply, explains extra checking information and symbolic p.
C1.3-P2-M02.guided_question: Look at `10110 | p`. Which part is the original data, and which is the added position?

C1.3-P2-M03.focus: Introduce the parity bit briefly and guide why it needs to depend on the original data.
C1.3-P2-M03.avoid: Do not reveal the complete data-dependence explanation before the reply; do not calculate p.
critical_checks: Question engages data dependence.
After reply, parity bit is defined as one data-dependent checking bit.
C1.3-P2-M03.guided_question: If the extra checking bit had nothing to do with the original data, how could it help us check that data?

C1.3-P2-M04.focus: Ask what goes wrong with an arbitrary choice when sender and receiver must agree.
C1.3-P2-M04.avoid: No binary parity calculation; no follow-up quiz.
critical_checks: Contrasts random choice with a shared data-dependent rule after learner reply.
C1.3-P2-M04.guided_question: What could go wrong if the sender picks the extra bit randomly but the receiver expects an agreed rule?

C1.3-P2-M05.focus: Conclude that both sides use one agreed rule to select and check the extra bit.
C1.3-P2-M05.avoid: No repetition of all previous questions, no p calculation.
critical_checks: Data dependence and shared rule are explicit without assigning 0 or 1 to p.

C1.3-P3-M01.focus: Compare the original payload alone with the same payload plus a symbolic checking position.
critical_checks: Payload alone versus payload with extra p position are contrasted.
p has no calculated numerical value here.

C1.3-P3-M02.focus: Contrast an arbitrary extra bit with one chosen from the payload using a shared rule.
critical_checks: Only data-dependent agreed rule has meaningful checking purpose.
No concrete p value.

C1.3-P3-M03.focus: Compare sender/receiver using the same rule against using different rules.
critical_checks: Explains the checking consequence of mismatched conventions.

C1.3-P3-M04.focus: Briefly synthesize redundancy, data dependence and shared-rule agreement.
C1.3-P3-M04.avoid: No invented even/odd example or numerical p.
critical_checks: Summarizes extra checking bit and agreed rule, with no early calculation.

C1.4-P1-M01.focus: State both parity conventions based on the count of ones in the complete frame, including parity bit.
critical_checks: Both rules count the appended parity bit.

C1.4-P1-M02.focus: Work even and odd sender constructions from the same payload, checking the complete-frame counts.
critical_checks: Even appends 1 to 10110 giving 101101 (4 ones).
Odd appends 0 giving 101100 (3 ones).

C1.4-P1-M03.focus: Work full-frame receiver pass and fail checks for even parity, then briefly confirm the odd example.
critical_checks: Counts all received bits including parity bit.
Even 101101 passes and 100101 fails; odd 101100 passes.

C1.4-P1-M04.focus: Explain what pass and fail mean and distinguish detecting, locating and correcting.
C1.4-P1-M04.avoid: No C2 theorem on odd/even numbers of flips.
critical_checks: Pass is not proof of no corruption.
Detection is different from locating or correcting.

C1.4-P2-M01.focus: Supply even and odd whole-frame rules directly before asking for calculations.
C1.4-P2-M01.avoid: No quiz until the guided sender move.
critical_checks: Definitions refer to all bits including parity bit.

C1.4-P2-M02.focus: Guide the sender through adding the correct even-parity bit to the fixed payload.
C1.4-P2-M02.avoid: Do not show the appended even bit or finished frame before the answer.
critical_checks: Guided question precedes even parity-bit reveal.
After reply, checks 101101 with four ones.
C1.4-P2-M02.guided_question: The data `10110` has three `1`s. For even parity, should we add `0` or `1`?

C1.4-P2-M03.focus: Guide odd parity for the same payload and briefly compare the rule.
C1.4-P2-M03.avoid: Do not show the odd parity bit or finished frame before the reply.
critical_checks: Learner gets one odd-parity construction question.
After reply, checks 101100 with three ones.
C1.4-P2-M03.guided_question: For the same `10110`, what bit should we add so the whole frame has an odd number of `1`s?

C1.4-P2-M04.focus: Guide a receiver to classify the even-rule check for a complete received frame, then give brief pass/odd comparisons.
C1.4-P2-M04.avoid: Do not reveal FAIL before learner replies; avoid a second full question cycle for odd parity.
critical_checks: Explains even 100101 fails and 101101 passes; odd 101100 passes.
Counts parity-bit position too.
C1.4-P2-M04.guided_question: Under even parity, does received `100101` pass or fail? Count its `1`s, including the last bit.

C1.4-P2-M05.focus: Explain what pass/fail can and cannot show; distinguish detecting, locating and correcting.
C1.4-P2-M05.avoid: No mastery check or C2 flip-count theorem.
critical_checks: Pass does not guarantee no error.
Detection, location and correction are distinct.

C1.4-P3-M01.focus: Introduce even and odd whole-frame rules using the same original payload as the shared comparison.
C1.4-P3-M01.avoid: Save append-bit calculations and completed frames for next comparison.
critical_checks: States both complete-frame rules and identical payload.

C1.4-P3-M02.focus: Compare both checked sender constructions for that same payload.
critical_checks: Contrasts append-1 even frame with append-0 odd frame and correct counts.

C1.4-P3-M03.focus: Contrast full received frames passing and failing the agreed rule, noting what a pass does not prove.
critical_checks: Full-frame even pass/fail results correct.
Pass does not prove no corruption.

C1.4-P3-M04.focus: Summarize how sender and receiver use the shared parity rule and how detection differs from location/correction.
C1.4-P3-M04.avoid: Do not introduce C2 multi-flip theorem.
critical_checks: Both sides use agreed convention.
Three operations distinguished; no bit-flip count theorem.
